answer: Sybil farms thrive on asynchronous work: one operator queues a hundred replies at leisure. Force liveness. At random moments, pair identities for a synchronous exchange, improvising replies to unscripted turns in seconds, like a sonnet answered line by line. A lone agent bends like a willow, following the thread; one operator behind ten mouths stalls, repeats itself, or lets sable silences pool where answers should be instant. Reward only identities sustaining distinct parallel exchanges: cloned attention cannot hold ten conversations at once, so each added identity dilutes the rest.
